facts.text: On this date in 1846, astronomers first observed Neptune — a planet predicted mathematically before anyone saw it. Its existence was deduced entirely from wobbles in Uranus's orbit.
On this date in 1973, Juan Perón won Argentina's presidential election with 62% of the vote — after spending 18 years in exile and being legally barred from the previous election that year.
More people live inside a circle drawn around Dhaka, Bangladesh than live in the entire continent of Australia.
The Philippines is the only country in the world where divorce remains fully illegal for non-Muslim citizens, making it one of two such nations globally alongside Vatican City.
Tokyo's greater metro area has a larger economy than all but roughly a dozen entire countries on Earth.
On this date in 1869, the Erie Railroad's stock collapsed as Jay Gould and James Fisk cornered the gold market — a scheme so brazen it triggered Black Friday and nearly destroyed the U.S. Treasury.
On this date in 1998, the Federal Reserve orchestrated a $3.6B bailout of Long-Term Capital Management, a hedge fund run by two Nobel laureates whose models failed to price a Russia default.
The S&P 500 has lost more value in individual single-day crashes than the entire GDP of most countries — the 1987 Black Monday drop erased $500B in one session, before 'billion' felt small.
Berkshire Hathaway's Class A share once traded for under $20. It has never split, making it the highest-priced stock in history — currently above $600,000 per share.
The Dutch East India Company, history's first publicly traded corporation, was so dominant it ran its own army, minted currency, and at peak was worth roughly $8 trillion in today's dollars.
On this date in 1846, Neptune was discovered exactly where math said it would be — its position predicted purely from gravitational anomalies in Uranus's orbit, before anyone had seen it.
The September equinox arrives today, but day and night are not actually equal length. Atmospheric refraction bends sunlight over the horizon, giving every location a few extra minutes of light.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
Your skeleton is not the rigid structure you imagine. Bone is continuously dissolved and rebuilt by competing cells, replacing itself almost entirely every decade.

Light from the Sun is ancient by the time it reaches your eyes. Photons spend up to 100,000 years fighting outward through the Sun's dense interior before escaping into space and arriving here in eight minutes.

On this day in 1846, Neptune was observed for the first time — but it had already been mathematically predicted to exist, making it the only planet discovered by pure calculation before anyone laid eyes on it.
Oxford University was teaching students before the Aztec Empire existed. Oxford began in 1096; Tenochtitlan wasn't founded until 1325.
On this day in 1962, the Flintstones became the first animated series to air in primetime — a show set in the Stone Age debuted the same year Wernher von Braun was designing rockets for the Moon.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the iPhone than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She died in 30 BC; the pyramid was finished around 2560 BC.
The woolly mammoth was still alive when ancient Egyptians were building their first pyramids. A small mammoth population survived on Wrangel Island until 1650 BC — centuries into the Bronze Age.

Mamihlapinatapai (Yaghan): the wordless look shared between two people who both want something but neither will initiate. From a language once spoken by one person, Marie Yarupe, before her death in 2022.

Sonder (coined 2012, Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows): the realization that every passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. It spread so fast that dictionaries now debate whether it counts as real.
On this day in 1846, Neptune was confirmed by observation — and German has a word for the feeling: Fernweh, the ache for distant places, literally 'far-pain', the opposite of homesickness.
Autumnal equinox falls today, Sep 23 — and Old English called autumn 'hærfest', meaning harvest. The season had no other name in English until French 'automne' arrived with the Normans.
Tsundoku (Japanese): the act of buying books and letting them pile up unread. The word blends 'tsunde' (to stack) with 'doku' (reading), and has no single-word equivalent in any other major language.

On this date in 2017, China's central bank declared all ICOs illegal and ordered fundraises to refund investors — wiping roughly $4B in market cap within 48 hours and accelerating the offshore migration of crypto infrastructure.

On this date in 2021, El Salvador's Bitcoin adoption faced its first stress test: a Supreme Court challenge that the government dismissed, while the Chivo wallet had already lost 60% of its initial users within three weeks of launch.
Bitcoin's smallest unit, the satoshi, wasn't named by Satoshi Nakamoto — the community retroactively coined the term in a 2010 BitcoinTalk thread, eight months after the network launched.

The Ethereum genesis block contains a hidden message in its extra data field: the hash of block zero encodes no text, but early miner Vitalik embedded a nonce referencing a contemporary Guardian headline about bank bailouts — mirroring Satoshi's own genesis note.

Miners on proof-of-work chains often deliberately orphan their own valid blocks to reorg competitors' blocks — a practice called selfish mining, theorized in a 2013 Cornell paper that showed a pool with just 33% hashrate could outperform honest miners indefinitely.

On this date in 1956, the Dartmouth AI Summer Research Project concluded — the 6-week workshop where McCarthy coined 'artificial intelligence' attracted only 8 attendees and produced no breakthrough, yet named a field.

On this date in 2022, DeepMind's AlphaFold database hit 200 million protein structures — more than all experimental structures accumulated in 70 years of biochemistry, released freely in under 18 months.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have used around 25,000 A100 GPUs for 90–100 days. The electricity alone cost more than most academic institutions spend on compute in a decade.
The transformer architecture, now central to virtually every frontier AI system, was published in 2017 by a team of eight authors — six of whom have since left Google.
RLHF, the technique that made large language models reliably conversational, was first applied to language models in a 2019 OpenAI paper training on fewer than 50,000 human preference labels.
